zh.summary: 依照使用者當下的決策安排資訊：主畫面保留必要欄位、檢核結果與復原方法，次要設定延後展開。
objectives: 區分可延後呈現的設定與必須直接顯示的工作狀態。
為輸入、處理中、缺漏及完成狀態設計下一步。
用同儕任務觀察檢查介面簡化是否真的有幫助。

sections.heading: 讓使用者在正確時間看見必要資訊
paragraphs: 這一課最重要的觀念：好的使用者介面，不是把資訊減到最少，而是讓使用者在正確的時間，看見正確的資訊，做出正確的決定。
想像你到醫院掛號、使用 ATM 提款，或在購物網站付款。你通常不想知道系統內部有幾台伺服器、資料庫如何運作、程式有哪些參數。你只想知道：

- 我現在需要做什麼？
- 系統目前正在做什麼？
- 有沒有問題？問題該怎麼解決？
- 我究竟完成了沒有？
這正是本課的三個核心觀念：Progressive Disclosure（漸進揭露）、Minimalist Design（極簡設計）和 Visibility of System Status（系統狀態可見性）。
原始教材以資料檢核網站為例，要求完成四種狀態的 Wireframe（介面線框圖），並透過實際任務觀察檢查設計。

sections.heading: 一、什麼是漸進揭露（Progressive Disclosure）？
paragraphs: 簡單說，就是先顯示現在需要的東西，等使用者需要更多功能時，再把它展開。
例如你想列印一份文件。

blocks.caption: 圖 1｜列印：基本與進階兩層
blocks.description: 兩張卡比較收合與展開；功能仍在，需要時可找到。列印是示意操作。

items.title: 一般列印畫面
items.body:
印表機：Office Printer

份數：1

紙張：A4

進階設定 ▸

列印

使用者一眼就能找到主要操作。

items.title: 展開進階設定後
items.body:
印表機：Office Printer

份數：1

紙張：A4

進階設定 ▾

雙面列印：關閉

縮放比例：100%

反向列印：關閉

列印

需要特殊功能時仍然找得到。

paragraphs: 這種設計沒有刪除功能，只是把功能分成兩個層次。
Nielsen Norman Group 的設計文章說明，漸進揭露可以降低初學者面對複雜選項的負擔，但關鍵是要正確區分主要功能和次要功能，而且進階功能必須容易找到。
以下三張補充圖分別呈現進階設定入口、基本／進階設定的安排，以及手風琴（Accordion）收合面板。它們是靜態線框示意，標示的操作不會修改設定。

blocks.caption: 圖 2｜設定頁的進階入口
blocks.description: 橘框標出進階入口；箭頭表示可前往下一層設定，不表示已執行變更。

items.title: 設定 Settings
items.body:
安全性 Security

密碼 Password｜變更 Change

items.title: 國家／地區設定 Country Settings
items.body: 一般設定入口 ›

items.title: 進階設定 Advanced Settings
items.body: 進階設定入口 ›

paragraphs: 圖 2 的橘框標示可發現的進階入口。一般設定仍可直接辨識；實際哪些項目屬於進階，取決於目標使用者與任務。

blocks.caption: 圖 3｜保留基本欄位，讓進階設定按需出現
blocks.description: 前後兩卡保留相同功能。右卡用清楚入口取代參考圖的淡化區；下方清單說明展開後可用的設定，不是停用欄位。

items.title: 調整前｜所有選項攤開
items.body:
基本設定 Basic Settings

公司名稱 Company Name：Enter company name

Email：Enter email

進階設定 Advanced Configuration

API Rate Limit：1000/hour

Webhook URL：https://…

Custom Headers：Authorization: Bearer…

Security Options

items.title: 調整後｜漸進揭露
items.body:
基本設定 Basic Settings

公司名稱 Company Name：Enter company name

Email：Enter email

進階設定 ▸

展開後可用：

API Rate Limit：1000/hour

Webhook URL：https://…

Custom Headers：Authorization: Bearer…

Security Options

paragraphs: 圖 3 保留公司名稱、Email 與進階 API 設定的對照。原參考圖將右側進階設定淡化；這裡改為明確的「進階設定 ▸」入口，避免以低對比或停用外觀誤導讀者。範例標頭只使用佔位文字，沒有真正的憑證。

blocks.caption: 圖 4｜手風琴面板：標題持續可見
blocks.description: 靜態結構示意：三個標題中，只有第二個面板展開。符號表示狀態，不是先後步驟；實際控制需支援鍵盤與展開狀態。

items.title: 標題一 Heading ▾
items.body: 已收合，保留標題。

items.title: 標題二 Heading ▴
items.body: 已展開：面板在手風琴展開時出現。

items.title: 標題三 Heading ▾
items.body: 已收合，保留標題。

paragraphs: 圖 4 的三個標題持續可見，只有中間面板顯示內容。向下／向上符號表示收合／展開狀態，不代表流程。NN/G 提醒收合也會增加尋找與操作成本；讀者需要連續閱讀的原理與必要狀態應直接顯示。本頁圖解及教學正文因此保持展開，只有文末參考答案使用原生收合。

sections.heading: 二、極簡設計（Minimalist Design）不是把東西全部藏起來
paragraphs: 想像你在機場看登機資訊螢幕。
你需要知道登機門、起飛時間，以及航班有沒有延誤。假如設計師認為畫面越乾淨越好，把「航班延誤」隱藏在詳細資訊頁面，你可能就會錯過重要通知。
這就是錯誤的極簡設計。
正確的極簡設計，是減少對當前任務無用的資訊，而不是減少所有資訊。
用下面這個判斷表：

blocks.caption: 表 1｜資訊應放在哪裡
rows: 目前任務不可缺少的資訊
影響安全、風險或下一步的資訊
少數情境才需要的功能
系統內部診斷或開發資訊

paragraphs: 例如線上銀行轉帳，收款帳號、金額、手續費及轉帳結果應該清楚呈現。資料庫連線池、API Timeout 設定等開發資訊，則不需要出現在一般使用者畫面上。
這也符合 Nielsen Norman Group 的「Aesthetic and Minimalist Design」原則：不相關的資訊會與真正重要的資訊爭奪使用者注意力。
記憶口訣：不影響當下決策的資訊可以延後；影響使用者判斷、風險或行動的資訊不能隨便隱藏。

sections.heading: 三、必要狀態：使用者必須知道系統現在發生什麼
paragraphs: 這是整堂課最容易被低估、但非常重要的部分。
假設你去 ATM 提款，按下「提款 5,000 元」之後，螢幕完全沒有反應。
你會怎麼想？
你可能懷疑自己沒有按到，於是再按一次。或者以為機器故障，準備離開。
真正的問題不一定是系統沒有處理，而是系統沒有告訴你正在處理。
這就是 Visibility of System Status（系統狀態可見性）。
一個介面至少要讓使用者理解「目前狀態、操作結果、可以採取的下一步」。
用四種狀態理解完整的操作流程：
以下使用一個虛構的文件檢核系統示範。使用者輸入三個欄位，系統檢查是否完整，確認後才能產生文件。

blocks.caption: 圖 5｜文件檢核的四種狀態
blocks.description: 四張卡是不同情境，並非每次操作必然經過的四個步驟。缺漏時補填；系統故障另提示安全重試；完成只代表本次資料檢核。

items.title: 狀態一：輸入
items.body:
等待使用者填寫資料

案件編號：A001

來源單位：甲部門

文件類型：尚未選擇

［檢查資料］

下一步：填寫並啟動檢查。

items.title: 狀態二：處理中
items.body:
已收到檢查請求

正在檢查資料…

請勿重複送出。

完成後將顯示檢查結果。

［檢查中，暫不可再送出］

下一步：等待結果；逾時則依提示處理。

items.title: 狀態三：缺漏
items.body:
已找到可修正的問題

缺少必要資料

「文件類型」尚未填寫。

已保留其他欄位。

［補填並重新檢查］

下一步：只修正缺漏，不必全部重填。

items.title: 狀態四：完成
items.body:
本次資料檢核已完成

三個必要欄位均已齊全

可以預覽或匯出。

注意：不代表正式受理。

［預覽］［匯出］

下一步：確認內容，再選擇匯出。

paragraphs: 這裡有兩個重要細節。
第一，資料缺漏與系統故障不是同一件事。缺少文件類型，應提示補資料；如果是伺服器無法連線，應提示系統檢查失敗、如何安全重試，而不是誤導使用者重新填寫資料。
第二，「完成」一定要說清楚完成了什麼。資料檢核通過，不代表政府機關正式收件；銀行文件生成成功，不代表授信審核通過；AI 診斷報告產生完成，也不代表醫師已經確認。
這是 UX 與系統業務規則（Business Rules）必須一致的地方。

sections.heading: 四、跨產業比較：同一原理可以怎麼應用？
paragraphs: 先看六種產業的當前決策，再比較哪些資訊可延後。

blocks.caption: 表 2｜跨產業資訊安排
rows: 商品價格、運費、付款結果、訂單狀態
商品內部編碼、進階推薦設定
科別、日期、看診號碼、掛號是否成功
系統連線診斷、管理者設定
收款人、帳號、金額、交易結果
運作狀態、危險警報、緊急停止
非必要的細部診斷參數
上傳狀態、分析進度、缺漏、結果
模型溫度、除錯日誌、輪詢參數
重大告警、風險、待處置事項
低階封包細節、開發偵錯資訊

paragraphs: 不過，有一個例外非常重要：資訊是否重要，取決於使用者的角色與當前任務。
對一般銀行客戶而言，API 診斷資訊不重要；但對正在排查轉帳系統故障的工程師而言，它可能是主畫面最重要的資訊。
因此，不能用同一套極簡介面服務所有角色。你必須先問：「這個畫面給誰用？他現在需要做什麼決定？」

sections.heading: 五、兩種容易混淆的設計：漸進揭露與分階段揭露
paragraphs: 這裡再補充一個原教材沒有大篇幅展開，但實務上很容易混淆的觀念：Staged Disclosure（分階段揭露）。

blocks.caption: 表 3｜兩種揭露的差別
rows: 先顯示常用功能，隱藏次要功能
把必要工作分成多個步驟
網購時依序填地址、付款、確認
使用者一定要展開後續畫面嗎？
降低單一步驟的資訊負荷

paragraphs: 兩者可以同時使用。例如購物網站把結帳分成三步驟，並且在運送設定那一步，額外提供「特殊配送選項」。
這種分法來自 Nielsen Norman Group 對兩類設計的區別。

sections.heading: 六、進階但非常重要：使用者修改資料後，舊結果怎麼辦？
paragraphs: 這是從 UI 設計進入軟體工程的關鍵。
假設使用者完成文件檢核，系統已顯示「三個欄位都完整」。但他之後把文件類型刪掉了。
此時如果畫面仍然顯示「檢核通過」，甚至仍然允許匯出，便出現一個問題：
畫面上的成功結果，已經不代表目前資料的真實狀態。
用流程圖來看：

blocks.caption: 圖 6｜資料改變後，兩種結果處理方式
blocks.description: 箭頭表示同一案例的資料變更。下方是互斥的錯誤／正確策略對照，不是兩個連續步驟。

items.title: 原始資料通過
items.body: 資料 A → 檢核通過 → 產生結果 A

items.title: 使用者修改資料
items.body: 資料 B；先前結果仍對應資料 A

items.title: 錯誤做法
items.body: 仍顯示結果 A 已通過，讓人誤以為資料 B 也通過。

items.title: 正確做法
items.body: 提示資料已變更，舊檢核失效，需要重新檢查。

paragraphs: 在軟體工程裡，這涉及狀態一致性（State Consistency）及驗證結果是否仍然有效。
一個實用的實作策略是：

blocks.heading: 版本比對示意
paragraphs: 3 與 3 相同時允許匯出；資料改為版本 4 後，舊的版本 3 驗證不再適用。此為狀態規則示意，實際匯出仍需後端原子化驗證。
blocks.code:
currentVersion = 3
validatedVersion = 3
→ 可以匯出

使用者修改資料：
currentVersion = 4
validatedVersion = 3
→ 不可直接匯出，需要重新檢核

paragraphs: 但要特別注意：前端把「匯出」按鈕隱藏，不等於資料真正安全。
如果有人直接呼叫後端 API，後端仍必須檢查資料是否完整、是否有權匯出，以及驗證結果是否對應到當前資料版本。
這也是原教材要求把「輸入變更後舊結果失效」寫進 `spec.md`，並加入測試的原因。

sections.heading: 七、易用與可近用：不能只靠顏色、圖示和提示字
paragraphs: 假設一個表單把錯誤欄位框成紅色，卻沒有說明文字。
有些人可能看不清楚顏色差異；有些人使用螢幕閱讀器；也有些人根本不知道紅框代表什麼。
因此：
不好的設計： 紅框加上一個驚嘆號。
比較好的設計： 在「文件類型」欄位附近顯示「必填欄位，請選擇文件類型」，必要時再搭配紅框。
同樣地，`placeholder`（欄位內的範例提示字）不能取代持續可見的欄位名稱（Label）。使用者開始輸入後，placeholder 往往就消失了。
W3C 的 WCAG 規範也要求不能只用顏色傳達資訊；對於會動態更新的系統狀態，還應讓輔助科技適當得知變化。

sections.heading: 八、如何驗證介面真的變好？不要只問「好不好看」
paragraphs: 這一節最重要的實作觀念，是將主觀印象轉換成可觀察的行為。
假設你做出文件檢核網站的 Wireframe，找一位不熟悉系統的人，給他一筆故意缺少文件類型的模擬資料。
請他完成這個任務：
「確認這份資料能不能交接。如果不能，請修正後匯出。」
在他操作時，你不要直接告訴他錯誤在哪裡，而是觀察他是否自行發現問題、會不會亂點設定、能否理解完成結果，以及修改資料後是否知道需要重新檢查。
可以用以下驗收矩陣，把抽象的 UX 品質轉成實際測試：

blocks.caption: 表 4｜候選驗收矩陣
rows: 能用自己的話說明目前進度
不需指引就能找到缺漏並修正
修正一個欄位不必重填全部
資料變更後不能沿用舊檢核結果
不靠顏色或滑鼠懸停也能理解

paragraphs: 這些是可供試驗的驗收條件，不是已實測的成果。一次同儕測試能發現問題，卻不能證明所有使用者都會有相同體驗。

sections.heading: 九、這一課實際要完成什麼成果？
paragraphs: 原始 M04-05 的交付要求，是四狀態 Wireframe，以及至少一項有觀察依據的介面修正。
最小完成版本可以是一份包含四個畫面的 SVG、Figma 設計稿或紙本草圖。每個畫面都應回答：使用者現在看見什麼、知道什麼、下一步可以做什麼。同時要說明資料變更如何讓舊結果失效，並留下修正前後的比較和匿名觀察紀錄。
你不必在這個階段先把完整前後端寫好。這一課的核心能力是：先確認互動與資訊安排是否合理，再投入軟體實作。

sections.heading: 十、理解檢核
paragraphs: 先不看答案，請嘗試下面三個問題。
最後記住這堂課的核心：
極簡設計，是減少不必要的負擔；漸進揭露，是安排資訊出現的時機；必要狀態，是讓使用者永遠知道自己處於什麼情況，以及下一步該怎麼做。
這三件事需要一起設計，才能讓一個軟體不只是「看起來簡單」，而是真正容易理解、操作與信任。

exercise.environment: 紙筆或繪圖工具；使用三個合成欄位的表單。
steps: 畫出輸入、處理中、缺漏或失敗、完成四種狀態，逐一寫出使用者下一步。
把診斷設定放到次要區，保留缺漏提示與完成定義；設計輸入變更後舊結果失效的方式。
請同儕依缺漏資料完成任務，只觀察並記錄阻礙，再修正一項介面設計。
exercise.expected: 四狀態 wireframe 與至少一項有觀察依據的修正；可用 SVG 作為交付格式。
exercise.check: 請試用者用自己的話說出目前狀態與下一步；核對是否可不靠顏色、懸停或他人指引完成。
exercise.cleanup: 保留去識別化觀察與修正前後版本；丟棄真實個資及非必要錄影。

readingGuide.goal: 區分可延後呈現的設定與必須直接顯示的工作狀態。
readingGuide.startingPoint: 紙筆或繪圖工具；使用三個合成欄位的表單。
readingGuide.route: 先讀原理與例子，再完成最小實作，最後核對理解檢核與參考解析。
readingGuide.output: 四狀態 wireframe 與至少一項有觀察依據的修正；可用 SVG 作為交付格式。

openChecks.prompt: 問題一｜概念辨識｜一個 AI 文件處理系統，主畫面有「上傳檔案、正在處理、處理失敗、模型溫度設定」。如果要採用漸進揭露，哪些內容應直接顯示？哪些可以延後？為什麼？
answer: 上傳、處理中及處理失敗直接影響當下任務，應清楚顯示，並說明失敗後如何重試。模型溫度通常可放進階設定；若使用者正要比較參數效果，則須依其角色與任務調整資訊層級。

openChecks.prompt: 問題二｜情境應用｜銀行轉帳畫面顯示「轉帳完成」，但其實只是請求送到銀行伺服器，交易尚未確認。這違反了什麼設計原則？你會如何修改畫面？
answer: 違反系統狀態可見性，也讓介面承諾超過業務實際結果。先顯示「請求已送出，等待銀行確認」，取得交易確認後才顯示「轉帳完成」；未確認或逾時時，提供查詢與安全重試指引，避免重複轉帳。

openChecks.prompt: 問題三｜工程實務｜一份 AI 分析報告檢核通過後，使用者修改了原始資料，但系統仍允許下載舊報告。除了修改 UI，你還需要在後端或測試加入什麼機制？
answer: 後端在匯出時檢查必填資料、目前使用者的匯出權限，以及驗證版本是否等於當前資料版本；需要重新檢核時拒絕沿用舊結果。測試至少包含先通過再修改／刪除欄位、直接呼叫 API、缺少權限與重新檢核後成功匯出；也要避免檢查與匯出間的資料變更造成競態。

en.summary: Arrange information around the user’s current decision: keep required fields, checking results and recovery visible, while deferring secondary settings.
objectives: Distinguish deferrable settings from work states that must remain directly visible.
Design next actions for input, processing, missing information and completion.
Observe peer tasks to check whether simplification helps.

readingGuide.goal: Distinguish deferrable settings from work states that must remain directly visible.
readingGuide.startingPoint: Paper or a drawing tool and a form with three synthetic fields.
readingGuide.route: Read the principles and examples, complete the small exercise, then compare your understanding with the checks and reference explanations.
readingGuide.output: A four-state wireframe and at least one observation-based revision, optionally delivered as SVG.

sections.heading: Show essential information at the right time
paragraphs: A useful interface puts the information needed for a sound decision in front of the user at the right time.

Imagine registering for a hospital appointment, withdrawing cash at an ATM or paying online. You usually do not need to know how many servers run the system, how its database works or which parameters its code accepts. You want answers to these questions:

- What do I need to do now?
- What is the system doing?
- Is something wrong, and how can I resolve it?
- Have I actually finished?
This lesson connects Progressive Disclosure, Minimalist Design and Visibility of System Status.
The original lesson uses a data-checking website. Its deliverables are wireframes for four states and a design check based on observing an actual task.

sections.heading: 1. What is progressive disclosure?
paragraphs: Show what the user needs now, and reveal additional functionality when it becomes relevant.
Consider printing a document.

blocks.caption: Figure 1 | Printing: basic and advanced levels
blocks.description: The cards compare collapsed and expanded states. Functions remain discoverable when needed. Print is a depicted action.

items.title: Basic print screen
items.body:
Printer: Office Printer

Copies: 1

Paper: A4

Advanced settings ▸

Print

The primary action is easy to find.

items.title: Advanced settings expanded
items.body:
Printer: Office Printer

Copies: 1

Paper: A4

Advanced settings ▾

Double-sided: Off

Scale: 100%

Reverse printing: Off

Print

Specialized functions remain discoverable.

paragraphs: The functionality remains available at two levels rather than being removed.

Nielsen Norman Group's design article explains that deferring advanced options can reduce the burden on beginners. The designer must distinguish primary from secondary functions and make the advanced functions easy to discover.

The following three figures show an advanced-settings entry, the arrangement of basic and advanced settings, and an Accordion panel. These are static wireframes; the depicted actions do not change settings.

blocks.caption: Figure 2 | A discoverable advanced-settings entry
blocks.description: The orange outline identifies the advanced entry. The chevron indicates another settings level, not an applied change.

items.title: Settings
items.body:
Security

Password | Change

items.title: Country Settings
items.body: General settings entry ›

items.title: Advanced Settings
items.body: Advanced settings entry ›

paragraphs: The orange outline in Figure 2 identifies a discoverable advanced entry. Other settings remain identifiable. Which settings belong in the advanced area depends on the intended user and task.

blocks.caption: Figure 3 | Keep basic fields visible and advanced settings available
blocks.description: Both cards retain the same functions. The right card replaces the faded reference with an explicit entry; its inventory describes available expanded settings, not disabled fields.

items.title: Before | All options shown
items.body:
Basic Settings

Company Name: Enter company name

Email: Enter email

Advanced Configuration

API Rate Limit: 1000/hour

Webhook URL: https://…

Custom Headers: Authorization: Bearer…

Security Options

items.title: After | Progressive disclosure
items.body:
Basic Settings

Company Name: Enter company name

Email: Enter email

Advanced settings ▸

Available when expanded:

API Rate Limit: 1000/hour

Webhook URL: https://…

Custom Headers: Authorization: Bearer…

Security Options

paragraphs: Figure 3 retains the comparison between company name, Email and advanced API settings. The reference fades advanced settings on the right; this rendition replaces that treatment with an explicit “Advanced settings ▸” entry so low contrast or a disabled appearance does not mislead the reader. The sample header is placeholder text, not a real credential.

blocks.caption: Figure 4 | Accordion: headings remain visible
blocks.description: Static structure: only the second of three panels is expanded. Symbols indicate states, not sequence. A working control needs keyboard access and an exposed expanded state.

items.title: Heading 1 ▾
items.body: Collapsed; the heading remains visible.

items.title: Heading 2 ▴
items.body: Expanded: the panel appears when the accordion is expanded.

items.title: Heading 3 ▾
items.body: Collapsed; the heading remains visible.

paragraphs: The three headings in Figure 4 remain visible, while only the middle panel shows its content. Down/up symbols indicate collapsed/expanded states, not a process. NN/G notes that collapsing content also increases discovery and interaction costs. Principles that readers need to follow continuously and essential status information should remain visible. This page therefore displays its figures and teaching body directly, using native disclosure only for the reference answers at the end.

sections.heading: 2. Minimalist design retains information needed for decisions
paragraphs: Imagine reading an airport departure display.
You need the gate, departure time and any delay. If a designer hides “Flight delayed” on a details page to make the screen cleaner, you could miss a critical notification.
That minimalist treatment removes information needed for the task.
Useful minimalism reduces information irrelevant to the current task while retaining what the user needs.
Use this decision table:

blocks.caption: Table 1 | Where information belongs
rows: Affects safety, risk or the next action
Display directly with a clear message
Function needed only in some situations
Put it in an administration or debugging interface

paragraphs: For example, an online bank transfer should clearly show the destination account, amount, fee and transfer result. Database connection pools and API Timeout settings need not appear on an ordinary customer's screen.
This follows NN/G's Aesthetic and Minimalist Design heuristic: unrelated information competes for attention with relevant information.
Remember: information that does not affect the current decision can wait; information affecting judgment, risk or action should not be casually hidden.

sections.heading: 3. Essential states: tell users what is happening
paragraphs: Status visibility deserves explicit design attention.
Suppose you press “Withdraw 5,000” at an ATM, and the screen does not respond.
What would you think?
You might suspect the press was missed and try again, or assume the machine has failed and leave.
The system may be processing the request without telling you.
This illustrates Visibility of System Status.
An interface should explain the current state, the outcome of an action and the next action available.
Understanding an operation through four states:
The fictional document-checking system below accepts three fields, checks completeness and allows document generation after confirmation.

blocks.caption: Figure 5 | Four states of document checking
blocks.description: The cards compare situations, not four mandatory sequential steps. Correct missing data; handle system failure with safe-retry guidance. Completion means this data check only.

items.title: State 1: Input
items.body:
Waiting for user input

Case ID: A001

Source unit: Department A

Document type: Not selected

[Check data]

Next: complete the fields and start checking.

items.title: State 2: Processing
items.body:
Check request received

Checking data…

Do not submit again.

The result will appear when checking finishes.

[Checking; resubmission unavailable]

Next: wait for the result; follow guidance if it times out.

items.title: State 3: Missing data
items.body:
A correctable problem was found

Required data is missing

Document type has not been entered.

Other fields have been retained.

[Complete and recheck]

Next: correct the omission without re-entering everything.

items.title: State 4: Complete
items.body:
This data check is complete

All three required fields are complete

Preview or export is available.

Note: this does not mean formal acceptance.

[Preview] [Export]

Next: confirm the content, then choose export.

paragraphs: Two details matter here.

First, missing data and system failure need different messages. A missing document type calls for completing the field. An unreachable server calls for an explanation that checking failed and instructions for safe retry, rather than telling users to re-enter data.

Second, “complete” needs a defined scope. Passing a data check does not mean an agency has formally received an application. Generating a bank document does not mean a loan has been approved. Producing an AI diagnostic report does not mean a clinician has reviewed it.
UX and the system's Business Rules must make the same promise.

sections.heading: 4. Applying the principle across industries
paragraphs: Compare the current decisions in six industries before deciding which information can wait.

blocks.caption: Table 2 | Information across industries
headers: Primary information that must remain visible
rows: Price, shipping cost, payment result, order status
Internal product codes, advanced recommendation settings
Specialty, date, queue number, registration outcome
Operating state, hazard alarms, emergency stop
Upload state, analysis progress, missing data, result
Model temperature, debug logs, polling parameters
Critical alerts, risks, items requiring action
Low-level packet details, development debugging information

paragraphs: There is an essential qualification: importance depends on the user's role and current task.
API diagnostics may be irrelevant to an ordinary bank customer but central to an engineer investigating a transfer-system failure.
A single minimalist interface cannot serve every role equally well. Ask: “Who uses this screen, and what decision do they need to make now?”

sections.heading: 5. Progressive disclosure and staged disclosure
paragraphs: Staged Disclosure is a related concept that the original lesson did not explore in detail and that is easy to confuse with progressive disclosure.

blocks.caption: Table 3 | Two disclosure patterns
rows: Show common functions first and defer secondary functions
Divide necessary work into several steps
Enter address, payment and confirmation during checkout
Must the user open the later screens?
Reduce information load within a single step

paragraphs: Both can coexist. A shop can divide checkout into three steps and offer optional “Special delivery options” within the shipping step.
NN/G distinguishes these two patterns in its progressive-disclosure article.

sections.heading: 6. When data changes, what happens to the old result?
paragraphs: This is where interface design meets software engineering.
Suppose the document check reports that all three fields are complete, and the user then deletes the document type.
If the screen still says “Check passed” and allows export, it creates a problem:
The successful result no longer describes the current data.
The diagram compares the alternatives:

blocks.caption: Figure 6 | Two ways to handle results after a data change
blocks.description: Arrows indicate a data change in one example. The lower cards compare alternative incorrect/correct strategies, not consecutive steps.

items.title: Original data passes
items.body: Data A → check passes → result A

items.title: User changes data
items.body: Data B; the previous result still refers to data A

items.title: Incorrect approach
items.body: Continue showing result A as passed, misleading users into thinking data B passed too.

items.title: Correct approach
items.body: Say that data has changed, the old check is invalid and rechecking is required.

paragraphs: This concerns State Consistency and whether a validation result is still valid.
A practical implementation strategy is:

blocks.heading: Version comparison example
paragraphs: Matching versions 3 and 3 allow export. After data becomes version 4, validation for version 3 no longer applies. This illustrates a state rule; actual export still needs an atomic backend check.
blocks.code:
currentVersion = 3
validatedVersion = 3
→ 可以匯出

使用者修改資料：
currentVersion = 4
validatedVersion = 3
→ 不可直接匯出，需要重新檢核

paragraphs: Hiding the export button in the frontend does not establish backend safety.
A caller can invoke the backend API directly. The backend must still check completeness, export permission and whether validation applies to the current data version.
This is why the original lesson asks for “input changes invalidate the old result” to be specified in spec.md and covered by tests.

sections.heading: 7. Usability and accessibility need more than color, icons and hints
paragraphs: Suppose a form gives an invalid field a red border but no explanation.
Some people cannot distinguish the colors, some use screen readers, and others simply do not know what the border means.
Compare these treatments:
Weak treatment: a red border and an exclamation mark.
Better treatment: “Required field: choose a document type” near that field, optionally accompanied by a red border.
A placeholder—the example or hint inside a field—does not replace a continuously visible Label. The placeholder often disappears as soon as the user types.

W3C's WCAG guidance requires information beyond color alone. Dynamic status messages should also be programmatically available so assistive technology can announce relevant changes without moving focus. The guidance on labels or instructions explains how users identify the input expected from them.

sections.heading: 8. Verify behavior as well as appearance
paragraphs: Translate impressions of quality into observable behavior.
After drawing the checking site's wireframe, ask someone unfamiliar with the system to use synthetic data deliberately missing a document type.
Give them this task:
“Check whether this data can be handed off. If it cannot, correct it and export it.”
Do not point out the missing field. Observe whether the person discovers it, searches unrelated settings, understands what completion means and realizes that changing data calls for another check.
Use an acceptance matrix to turn UX quality into testable observations:

blocks.caption: Table 4 | Proposed acceptance matrix
rows: Can explain the current progress in their own words
Finds and corrects the omission without guidance
Correcting one field does not require re-entering everything
Changed data cannot reuse the old validation result
Can understand without relying on color or mouse hover

paragraphs: These are proposed acceptance conditions, not measured outcomes. One peer session can expose problems but cannot establish that all users will have the same experience.

sections.heading: 9. Deliverables for this lesson
paragraphs: The original M04-05 deliverables are a four-state Wireframe and at least one interface revision grounded in an observation.

A minimal complete version can be an SVG containing four screens, a Figma design or paper sketches. Each screen should explain what the user sees, what they know and what they can do next. Explain how changed data invalidates the old result, and retain an anonymous observation record and a before/after comparison.
You do not need a complete frontend and backend at this stage. Check the interaction and information arrangement before investing in implementation.

sections.heading: 10. Understanding check
paragraphs: Try the three questions below before opening the reference answers.
The lesson connects three responsibilities:
Minimalism reduces unnecessary burden; progressive disclosure schedules when information appears; essential states tell users where they are and what they can do next.
Designing these together helps people understand, operate and trust a system that appears simple.

exercise.environment: Paper or a drawing tool and a form with three synthetic fields.
steps: Draw input, processing, missing-information/failure and complete states, specifying the user’s next action for each.
Move diagnostics to a secondary area while retaining errors and the completion definition. Design invalidation of old results after input edits.
Have a peer perform the missing-input task. Observe and record barriers, then revise one interface decision.
exercise.expected: A four-state wireframe and at least one observation-based revision, optionally delivered as SVG.
exercise.check: Ask the participant to explain current state and next action in their own words. Check whether completion can rely on more than color, hover or another person’s guidance.
exercise.cleanup: Retain de-identified observations and before/after versions. Discard real personal data and unnecessary recordings.

openChecks.prompt: Question 1 | Concept identification｜An AI document system's main screen contains “Upload file”, “Processing”, “Processing failed” and “Model temperature”. With progressive disclosure, which items should remain visible and which can wait? Why?
answer: Upload, processing and processing failure affect the current task and should remain visible, including recovery instructions. Model temperature can usually go in advanced settings. If the task is to compare parameter effects, adjust the information hierarchy for that role and task.

openChecks.prompt: Question 2 | Applying the principle｜A bank-transfer screen says “Transfer complete” when only the request has reached the bank's server and the transaction is unconfirmed. Which design principle does this violate, and how would you change the screen?
answer: It violates visibility of system status and promises more than the business outcome establishes. Show “Request sent; awaiting bank confirmation” first, and “Transfer complete” only after confirmation. For an unconfirmed or timed-out request, provide status lookup and safe-retry guidance to avoid duplicate transfers.

openChecks.prompt: Question 3 | Engineering practice｜An AI report passes validation. The user then changes the original data, but the system still allows the old report to be downloaded. Alongside changing the UI, what mechanisms should the backend and tests include?
answer: At export, the backend checks required data, the current user’s export permission and equality of the validated and current data versions. Reject reuse when revalidation is needed. Tests cover passing then changing/deleting a field, direct API calls, missing permission and successful export after revalidation. Also prevent a race in which data changes between validation and export.
